posts.author: lunarrosecrow
posts.body:
Forgive me moderators if this is the wrong section for this question it has been a very long time since I've posted on the forums i apologize in advanced if I've messed up.
Beyond that I'd like to ask the other game developers a simple question. Does your cast of playable party members need to be ethnically diverse to be interesting or engaging? I'm currently developing a fantasy series with a dozen of different races but the first game is centered around the humans as they currently dominate the kingdoms until later games will having to many of the sane race make them boring even if the characters have distinctly different personalities, goals, upbringing, and designs?
I'm afraid to many humans might make my game seem bland in a way if you're fighting the other cool races but can't play as any of them besides 2 or 3. Are these good questions or am I overthinking it?

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
No, it's not a requirement. I don't play FF1 or Dragon Quest and think I really need other races to play as.
Different races/species can be a way to add new mechanics but so are things like jobs and classes.

My game's party so far has a human, an elf and an orc. The larger game world also has goblins which are friendly creatures, but not widely accepted.
Personally I have never had a single thout about the races of a game. Like having some cool fantasy races certainly is a plus in most cases, but if it was just humans in this worls, that's just how it is.

posts.author: Timeline_man
posts.body:
My own game world only has humans. It's good to remember at least that humans are also diverse. I obviously don't know your world, but if humans are all over the place, they probably have separate groups of themselves? That means they probably have distinct cultural ideas from each other, so they'd have different aesthetics born from the places they inhabit and the lives they've lived.
Basically, just don't make the humans boring and they'll already be pretty diverse. And if your story has your characters excluding other races, make sure that the reasons are well communicated and play into the story you have, players looking at the cast with disappointment about the diversity will have to engage with the story and understand why things are like that, although again, obviously, I don't know what kind of story or world you have going on.
